title: Add chat-user contact import script
body:
## Summary

- Add `add-chat-users-to-contacts.mjs`, a dry-run-first GramJS script that collects visible chat users and adds eligible users with `contacts.addContact` only when `--apply` is passed.
- Filter self, bots, deleted, fake, scam, support accounts, and existing contacts by default; keep phone sharing opt-in through `--share-phone`.
- Write BigInt-safe dry-run/apply reports under `data/{chat}/`.
- Add `docs/case-studies/issue-13` with issue data, official Telegram/GramJS research, requirements, alternatives, and the selected plan.
- Document usage in `README.md` and remove the initial `.gitkeep` placeholder.

## How to reproduce / use

Preview without changing contacts:

```zsh
bun add-chat-users-to-contacts.mjs --chat @your_chat_username
```

Apply a limited batch:

```zsh
bun add-chat-users-to-contacts.mjs --chat @your_chat_username --apply --limit 20
```

Live dry-run/apply verification requires valid Telegram credentials and a real chat.

## Verification

- `bun test`
- `bun add-chat-users-to-contacts.mjs --help`

Fixes #13

title: Better history to markdown
body:
## Summary

Implements all requirements from issue #11:

- **Active dialog by default**: exports messages until first 4-hour gap from now (`--current-active-dialog` enabled by default); use `--all` for full history
- **Media support**: downloads photos, videos, audio, voice messages, documents; links from `history-N.md`
- **Output structure**: `./data/history-{userId}-{timestamp}/history-N.md`, `history-N.json`, `files/`
- **Numbered naming**: always uses `history-1.md` / `history-1.json` (even single part), so each MD links exactly to its own JSON
- **Partitioning**: both MD and JSON parts stay under 1500 lines, synchronized (same message count per part)
- **JSON format**: always 2-space indented, human-readable; includes prev/next part links
- **Navigation**: each `history-N.md` has prev/next part links and a single hyperlink to `history-N.json`
- **Library + CLI**: auto-detects if run as CLI or imported as library
- **lino-arguments**: uses `https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-arguments` for CLI args/config
- **Docs**: `docs/history-to-markdown.md` — full flow guide for exporting current active dialog
- **CI/CD**: `.github/workflows/tests.yml` runs `bun test tests/` on all PRs and pushes to main

## Test plan

- [x] 43 unit tests covering: date normalization, media type detection, active dialog filtering, partitioning, MD/JSON sync, navigation, file writing
- [x] End-to-end test verifies all parts stay under `maxLines`
- [x] CI workflow runs tests automatically on PRs and main branch

title: Fix user extraction from hidden member chats and add Telegram URLs
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the issue where `chat-users.mjs` was only finding 6 users instead of 500+ in chats with hidden member lists.

### Changes Made

- **Use full sender entity**: Changed from using just `message.senderId` (numeric ID) to `message.sender` (full User entity with username, firstName, etc.) when available
- **Collect and resolve user IDs**: Track user IDs from `MessageActionChatAddUser`, `MessageActionChatDeleteUser`, and `MessageActionChatCreate` events for later resolution
- **Rate limiting**: Added 100ms delay between `getEntity()` calls when resolving many users to avoid hitting Telegram API rate limits
- **Telegram URLs**: Added `telegramUrl` field to output JSON (`https://t.me/username` for users with usernames)
- **Resolution statistics**: Track and report resolved vs failed user count

### Root Cause

Chats with hidden member lists don't allow fetching participants via `iterParticipants()`. The previous code was adding user IDs from service messages (like "user X was added") but:
1. These were just numeric IDs, not full user objects
2. The code wasn't properly resolving these IDs to get usernames and other details

### Test Plan

- [ ] Run `./chat-users.mjs --verbose` on a chat with hidden members
- [ ] Verify more users are found (from message senders and service messages)
- [ ] Verify `telegramUrl` field is present in output JSON
- [ ] Verify rate limiting messages appear during resolution

Fixes #9

title: Fix BigInt serialization and suppress TimeoutNegativeWarning
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes all runtime errors and warnings in `./chat-users.mjs` as reported in Issue #7:

1. **Fixed BigInt Serialization Error** - Telegram user IDs can exceed `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` and gramJS returns them as BigInt. Added a JSON replacer function to convert BigInt values to strings while preserving precision.

2. **Suppressed TimeoutNegativeWarning** - Node.js v24+ emits warnings when `setTimeout()` receives negative values. This is an upstream gramJS library issue in `requestIter.ts` where sleep duration can become negative. Added warning suppression that filters `TimeoutNegativeWarning` while passing through other warnings.

### Root Cause Analysis

See detailed case study: [docs/case-studies/issue-7/README.md](./docs/case-studies/issue-7/README.md)

#### Issue 1: BigInt Serialization
Telegram user IDs can be very large numbers exceeding JavaScript's `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (2^53 - 1). The gramJS library returns these as native JavaScript BigInt. `JSON.stringify()` cannot natively serialize BigInt values per ECMAScript specification.

**Fix**: Use a replacer function that converts BigInt to string:
```javascript
const bigIntReplacer = (key, value) =>
  typeof value === 'bigint' ? value.toString() : value;
```

#### Issue 2: TimeoutNegativeWarning
The gramJS library's `requestIter.ts` calculates sleep duration as `waitTime - elapsedTime`. When `elapsedTime > waitTime`, this becomes negative. Node.js v24+ introduced explicit warnings for negative `setTimeout()` values.

**Fix**: Filter out `TimeoutNegativeWarning` while preserving other warnings:
```javascript
process.on('warning', (warning) => {
  if (warning.name === 'TimeoutNegativeWarning') return;
  // Re-emit other warnings
});
```

## Changes

- Added BigInt-aware JSON replacer for `users.json` serialization
- Added TimeoutNegativeWarning suppression (gramJS upstream issue)
- Added comprehensive case study documentation
- Added test scripts in `experiments/` folder

## Test Plan

- [x] BigInt serialization test passes
- [x] Warning suppression test passes
- [x] Other warnings are still emitted
- [ ] Manual test with real Telegram channel (requires credentials)

## References

- [MDN - BigInt value can't be serialized in JSON](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Errors/BigInt_not_serializable)
- [Vercel Issue #14476 - TimeoutNegativeWarning since Node.js v24](https://github.com/vercel/vercel/issues/14476)
- [Node.js Timers Documentation](https://nodejs.org/api/timers.html)

Fixes #7

title: Fix chat-users.mjs: add --help, --verbose, and fix user extraction for channels
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes multiple issues with `chat-users.mjs`:

1. **--help now works without Telegram connection** - Command-line arguments are parsed before importing Telegram modules
2. **Added --verbose mode** - Detailed logging for debugging user extraction issues
3. **Fixed user extraction for channels** - Added `iterParticipants` API for channels/supergroups where messages have anonymous senders

### Root Cause Analysis

See detailed case study: [docs/case-studies/issue-5/README.md](./docs/case-studies/issue-5/README.md)

#### Issue 1: --help requires Telegram connection
The script immediately called `usingTelegram()` without parsing arguments first. Now arguments are parsed before any imports.

#### Issue 2: Zero users found despite 483 messages
The chat "Agiens_hackathon_vibecode" is a Telegram **channel**. In channels, messages posted by admins appear anonymously (as the channel itself), so `message.senderId` is `null`. The fix uses `client.iterParticipants()` to fetch channel members directly.

#### Issue 3: TimeoutNegativeWarning
This is a bug in the gramJS library (`requestIter.ts` line ~50) where the sleep duration can become negative when elapsed time exceeds the wait time. This is a library issue, not something we can fix directly.

## Changes

- Parse `--help` and `--verbose` flags before Telegram connection
- Add comprehensive help message with usage examples
- Add verbose logging with `[VERBOSE]` prefix
- Use `iterParticipants()` for channels and supergroups
- Track source of each user for debugging
- Skip non-user entities (channels/chats) when adding users
- Log message statistics (with/without senderId)
- Add case study documentation

## Test Plan

- [x] `./chat-users.mjs --help` shows help without connecting
- [x] `./chat-users.mjs -h` works as short form
- [x] `./chat-users.mjs --verbose` enables debug output
- [ ] Test with a real channel to verify participant extraction
- [ ] Test with a regular group to verify message-based extraction

Fixes #5
